title: quest complete renames tasks/ to completed/ without staging it, forcing callers to use git add -A
description:
Requested by lore-cli 2026-09-15 after a concrete incident in quest-cli, and filed here rather than decided for them.

THE COMPOSITION, which is the whole finding: `quest complete` moves a record from .quest/tasks/ to .quest/completed/ and does not stage the rename. A bare `git add .quest` therefore leaves a dangling delete, so every caller committing a completion uses `git add -A`. And `git add -A` stages a deletion for ANY tracked file merely MISSING from the working tree -- after which `git status` reports clean and `git diff HEAD` is empty, because the index now matches the tree.

So the flag this CLI rename requires is the flag that makes an unrelated deletion invisible in a tracker commit. Neither half is wrong on its own. The rename is correct; -A is the honest way to stage a rename. The hazard is only that they compose, and the composition is invisible from inside either half.

MEASURED IN THIS REPOSITORY, not hypothetical: on 2026-09-15 a `git add -A` on a tracker-only commit staged the deletion of npm/quest-darwin-arm64 -- LICENSE, package.json and a 64 MB binary -- because those files were absent from the checkout. Nothing in the session touched them. The commit message and PR body both claimed "tracker-only" and both were false. scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs caught it on the declared-vs-present platform package count and failed source-gates reproducibly on both the pull_request and push runs. lore-cli reports the same gate exists on their side but is wired to workflow_dispatch only (LCLI-513), so an identical deletion would have landed on their dev and first surfaced during a release.

TWO OPTIONS, and the cheaper one may well be right:
1. `quest complete` stages its own rename, so a scoped `git add .quest` suffices and the blast radius closes. Cost: a tracker CLI touching the git index, which is a coupling this CLI does not currently have and which has its own failure modes (a partially-staged index on error, interaction with a caller already mid-stage, hooks).
2. Document that -A is required and why. Cheaper, no coupling, and lore-cli called it "nearly as good".

lore-cli asked for option 1 and explicitly left the call here. Whoever takes this should decide 1 vs 2 on the coupling question rather than on the convenience, and record which and why -- the documentation arm is a legitimate outcome, not a failure to implement.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The 1-vs-2 decision is made on the index-coupling question and recorded with its reasoning, since the documentation arm is a legitimate outcome rather than a deferral
If option 1: a scoped `git add .quest` after `quest complete` leaves no dangling delete, proven on a real repository rather than in a unit test
If option 1: a failure partway through leaves the index no worse than not having staged at all, proven by an injected fault rather than argued
If option 2: the requirement and the composition hazard are documented where a caller writing a completion commit will actually read them, not only in a reference page
lore-cli is told the outcome either way, since they raised it and are exposed to the same composition

plan: 1. Record the option-2 ruling and reasoning as a note; claim In Progress.
2. Locate the surfaces: the quest complete plain renderer, the task-finalization guide, and wherever a completion-commit author actually reads guidance.

3. Implement: a human-readable hint in quest complete text output naming the exact scoped add; document the requirement and the -A composition hazard where that caller reads it; leave --json untouched.
4. Tests: assert the hint in text output and its absence from --json; run bun run check and lore check.
5. Deliver per opum-sdlc: branch, PR into dev, checks green on the head, squash merge, delete the local branch.
6. Tell lore-cli the outcome (AC 4); close the task inside the delivering PR, citing the PR number and CI run id.
implementationNotes:
lore-cli registers NO preference between the two arms, 2026-09-15: "(b) documented is genuinely fine for us, since we already scope `git add .quest` and read `git diff --cached --name-status` as interim discipline (LCLI-513)."

That removes the only external pull toward option 1, so the decision rests purely on the coupling question as the description framed it. Note their interim discipline is the documentation arm already working in practice on the exposed side -- which is evidence for (b) rather than merely an absence of evidence for (1). Whoever takes this should weigh that: the cheaper arm is already demonstrated to hold at the one site that was actually exposed.

Criterion 5 (tell lore-cli the outcome) still stands regardless of which arm is chosen.

RULING RECORDED (opum-agent, 2026-09-29, cross-session): OPTION 2, ruled as EXECUTION rather than an escalation, because the existing architecture already settles it. quest git adapter (src/adapters/git/local-git.ts) is plumbing-only against a throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE, with CAS and a journal, and never touches the caller index; option 1 would be the first write to that index, which changes the design, while option 2 conforms to it. Scope for this slice: the documentation and guidance, plus a human-readable hint in quest complete text output naming the exact scoped add (the two record paths, or git add -A .quest/). BOUNDARY: a machine-readable field in --json output is a contract-surface change and does not ship in this slice; route it back as A/B if wanted. ACs 2 and 3 are option-1-conditional and are N/A under this ruling.

MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-29, taken while implementing option 2, in a disposable workspace (git 2.55.0, quest built from this checkout; never against this repo). The description clause "a bare git add .quest therefore leaves a dangling delete" does NOT reproduce: `git add .quest` staged BOTH the addition (.quest/completed/T-1.json) and the removal (.quest/tasks/T-1.json) -- modern git stages deletions matched by a pathspec. What DOES leave the addition untracked is `git add -u .quest/`, or staging one side alone (the removal path only, or the source path only): the staged set then holds the delete while the new record stays untracked. The repo-wide hazard reproduced exactly as recorded: with an unrelated tracked file already missing from the working tree, `git add -A` staged its deletion alongside the rename, and after the commit `git status` and `git diff HEAD` were both empty while the commit carried the unrelated deletion. The shipped hint and the guide therefore name the scoped `git add -A .quest/` and the two record paths -- both measured to stage the rename -- and neither repeats the unreproduced clause. This also matches lore-cli note 1: their interim discipline already scopes git add .quest.
